title: Socratic checklist — protocol & registration (方案与注册)
rationale: Before the protocol freezes, the agent audits the design itself. Answers are recorded; the gate checks completeness. Sources are chapter/item-level references, not page numbers.

items.question: Is every protocol element traceable to the Review Question Certificate primitives (population, intervention, comparator, outcome, timing, setting)?
items.rationale: A protocol that drifts from the certificate breaks the derivation chain that Stage 0 established.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 items 4-7; Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.3 (defining the criteria)
items.answer_format: element-by-element mapping certificate -> protocol, with any deviation justified

items.question: Is the estimand of the meta-analysis stated in terms of population, treatment conditions, and outcome, and does the pooling rule match it?
items.rationale: Pooling across incompatible estimands is the classic synthesis error; the estimand must be declared before data are seen.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.2 (determining the scope); ICH E9(R1) estimand framework
items.answer_format: estimand sentence + the analysis method(s) that target it

items.question: Are outcome definitions, measurement time points, and the effect measure chosen before data collection, with a hierarchy for multiple measures per outcome?
items.rationale: Outcome switching and selective reporting are driven by post-hoc choice; a frozen hierarchy prevents it.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.6 (choosing effect measures); MECIR
items.answer_format: outcome table with time points, measures, and the hierarchy rule

items.question: Is the registration or registration-decision documented, with the protocol frozen before searching begins?
items.rationale: Unregistered post-hoc protocols are a recognized source of selective reporting.
items.answer_format: PROSPERO number or documented decision not to register + freeze hash of the protocol file

items.question: Does the protocol state which analyses are prespecified versus exploratory, and the rule that distinguishes them?
items.rationale: Exploratory analyses must be labeled so conclusions cannot silently rest on them.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.10 (analysing data and undertaking meta-analyses); PRISMA 2020 item 13d
items.answer_format: two lists + the labeling rule that will be enforced at reporting

items.question: Does the protocol define the statistical model, heterogeneity handling, and sensitivity analyses, including how to proceed when heterogeneity is extreme?
items.rationale: Model choice made after seeing heterogeneity inflates false-positive synthesis conclusions.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.10 (heterogeneity and random-effects); MECIR
items.answer_format: model + I2/tau2 reporting + pre-specified sensitivity set + I2>=75% fallback

items.question: Does the protocol specify how missing data, missing results, and unpublished studies will be handled, including the reporting-bias assessment plan?
items.rationale: Missing evidence is the largest threat to synthesis validity and must have a precommitted plan.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.13 (assessing risk of bias due to missing results); PRISMA 2020 item 14
items.answer_format: missing-data rules + contour-enhanced funnel / selection-model plan

items.question: Does the protocol record the AI-mode (which stages are AI-first, which require the human responsibility gate) and the mode's limitations?
items.rationale: AI-assisted reviews must disclose division of labor and where human accountability attaches.
items.source: MetaWingman AI-first execution boundary (SKILL.md); PRISMA 2020 item 26 (competing interests) as disclosure analogue

items.question: Is the amendment procedure defined: what counts as a protocol amendment, who approves it, and how the version history is kept?
items.rationale: Undocumented amendments are indistinguishable from selective reporting.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 item 24c (describe and explain any amendments)
items.answer_format: amendment threshold + approval path + version log location

items.question: Which single protocol element would most change the review's conclusion if it were altered?
items.rationale: Naming the load-bearing element focuses sensitivity analyses where they matter.
items.answer_format: one element + the sensitivity analysis that tests it
